principle: Use externally supported form/range information to constrain sensitivity worlds. Do not promote cycling literature values to exact Japanese-keirin rider truth and do not tune ranges from candidate performance.

anchors.observations: track example fitted seated 0.192 and standing 0.253 m^2; cited reference 0.21 and 0.27 m^2

CdA_m2.rule: Posture/anthropometry/position dependent. No single CdA may be assigned to all riders.

anchors.observations: review: leader typically <=5% drag reduction; second ~30-45%; subsequent ~35-55%
competitive male cyclists showed leader/drafter interaction and large individual variation
second and subsequent positions up to ~40% drag reduction in team-pursuit CFD

drafting_drag_multiplier.rule: Spacing, lateral position, posture, leader/drafter geometry and wind can materially alter the benefit. Multiplier is a sensitivity range, not a line bonus.

anchors.observations: elite track sprint cohorts around 1537±307 and 1541±389 W
world-class/elite male sprint cyclists Pmax 1894±351 W

peak_mechanical_power_W.rule: Do not assign this broad support uniformly to Japanese keirin classes. Rider/class/form conditioning remains unresolved.

anchors.observations: solo bicycle literature summarized mean chain-drive efficiencies in 97-99% range; up to 98.6% in cited steady-state tests

drivetrain_efficiency.rule: Fixed-gear keirin drivetrain may differ; keep as sensitivity support until equipment-specific evidence exists.

anchors.observations: example cycling power model uses Crr=0.002
track model states rolling resistance depends on tyre characteristics and instantaneous slip/camber; careful measurement required

rolling_resistance_coefficient.rule: Do not execute a Japanese-keirin Crr point truth from the 0.002 reference alone.

explicit_non_admissions: No fixed drafting percentage by line position
